editorNote: Halloween week finds personal computing wedged between serious office software and games that are becoming household shopping-list items. The magazine rack is full of CP/M, IBM PC, Apple II, Atari, and Commodore clues, while the entertainment counter keeps pulling buyers toward cartridges, arcades, and computer games.
morningLine: On the desk this week: the October 25 InfoWorld, Apple II game lists, First Blood at the box office, and Men at Work on top of the Hot 100.

lead.headline: Magazine Rack Makes the Micro Feel Like a Storefront
lead.summary: The October 25 InfoWorld issue shows the business side of the microcomputer boom: IBM PC, Apple, CP/M, databases, word processors, printers, modems, and spreadsheet names all sharing the same weekly trade-paper vocabulary. For a home buyer or small-office manager, the late-October computer counter is no single machine; it is a messy shelf of hardware, software, peripherals, and promises.
